t.name: Oval Pass Trail #1259.13
t.description: This steep 1 mile trail connects Oval Pass with the Summit Trail #1259. You’ll find beautiful views with wildflowers (in spring and summer) and larch trees as Oval Pass Trail goes through a sub-alpine basin within the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.

t.name: Eagle Pass Trail
t.description: This 1.2 mile trail starts at the top of Eagle Pass at 7,250 feet elevation and drops down almost 800 feet to Summit Trail #1259. The trail goes through a sub-alpine basin full of larch trees. The tread may not be obvious going through meadows.

t.name: West Fork Buttermilk Trail
t.description: This 9.5 mile forested trail is within Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness climbs to 7,480 feet at Fish Creek Pass where it connects with Fish Creek Trail #1248. Opportunities to climb nearby Star and Courtney Peaks. Star Lake is just beyond the pass.

t.name: Scaffold Ridge/Oval Peak Trail
t.description: The Scaffold Ridge Trail #436 begins at Forest Road 4300-560 and follows Scaffold Ridge Trail until it ends at West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail, about 1 mile north of Fish Pass. This trail is no longer maintained and can be hard to find and follow.

t.name: East Fork Buttermilk Trail
t.description: Thia trail is an easy route up until the last mile to the pass, which is strenuous. This forested hike is cool during the hot summer, with limited views until near Hoodoo Pass and Hoodoo Basin.

t.name: Libby Creek Trail
t.description: A steep 5.3 mile trail entering the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness, reaching 7,620 feet elevation, and arriving at the scenic destination of Libby Lake.

t.name: Eagle Creek Trail
t.description: This trail provides access to Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness and is a good alternative to more popular lake trails, with good meadow grazing for stock. The trail on the hillside above Eagle Creek is through forest most of the way.

t.name: Oval Creek Trail
t.description: The trail is steep in several sections and traverses fragile soils above 6800 feet. Most of this trail was burned over in the 2018 Crescent Fire and much of the trail is dry and dusty during the summer.

t.name: Twisp River Trail
t.description: The Twisp River Trail is a great early season trail for mountain biking, horseback riding, and hiking. The trail meanders generally up and down route along the hillside above the Twisp River.

t.name: Williams Creek Trail
t.description: The trail climbs moderately through forest into Lake-Chelan Sawtooth Wilderness to Williams Lake. It then travels across shale and talus slopes and through an old burned area. Trail ends at the lake and sports beautiful alpine larch colors in the fall.

t.name: Slate Lake Trail
t.description: The Slate Lake Trail is steep for the first 3 miles; last 2 miles easier through forest and meadows to Slate Lake. Excellent views of the Twisp River drainage and rugged peaks of Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness. No water near the trail, so come prepared.

t.name: War Creek Trail
t.description: The War Creek Trail #408 is a historic route that follows War Creek within Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness to a high pass that has wonderful views of the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Mountains range.
